decisions.reason: As a mainstream organic sliced-meat extension, it likely performs close enough to aspiration levels for a large firm to keep it while the organic range develops.
Organic Kasseler is somewhat narrower than ham but still fits the strategic organic assortment, so management would likely retain it unless results were clearly below aspiration.
Pepper-coated organic salami is a familiar variant in a proven category, making it more likely than the others to satisfy aspiration levels and stay in the line.
Presented as an exotic aspic specialty for the service counter, it appears the most trial-like and most likely to fall short of aspiration, so its resources would be better redeployed.
Fennel-flavoured sliced salami is a relatively niche taste in the German market and would be a natural candidate for pruning if sales trailed standard salami variants.
Liver pâté with veal is a premium niche in a mature category, so if its results are only middling management would likely shift capacity back to stronger established products or new projects.
